title: Chapter XXVIII
summary: Set down at Whitcross without money or possessions, Jane spends nights on the moor and searches unsuccessfully for any honest work. Hunger reduces her to begging and exposes how completely a person without name, references, or property can fall outside social trust. Near death in the rain, she reaches Moor House, where Hannah refuses the apparent vagrant but St. John Rivers insists on examining the case. His sisters Diana and Mary feed Jane with instinctive compassion, and she enters under the alias Jane Elliott.
events: Jane loses her parcel and becomes absolutely destitute at Whitcross.
She sleeps outdoors, seeks work, begs for food, and is repeatedly refused without blaming those who distrust her.
Jane collapses at the door of Moor House after Hannah denies lodging.
St. John admits her, while Diana and Mary feed and shelter her.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Experiences material freedom at its most brutal: moral independence without social identity leaves her exposed to starvation.

characters.name: St. John Rivers
characters.development: Introduced through disciplined, investigative charity rather than spontaneous warmth.

characters.name: Diana and Mary Rivers
characters.development: Introduced as intellectually alive women whose immediate sympathy restores Jane to human fellowship.

themes: nature as refuge but not livelihood
death and rebirth at a threshold

threads.text: Jane's flight costs her every external protection but preserves the integrity for which she fled.
The Rivers household offers a new community whose relation to Jane is not yet known.
Jane conceals her identity as Jane Elliott to prevent Rochester from finding her.
